Subject: Step-up commit, surge allocation and invoice timing for May–Aug ramp

Rajat — thanks again for the call yesterday. I sketched a concrete monthly commit plan (attached) so your finance and engineering teams can validate expected spend and surge capacity during the product launch window. Key points: 

- Commit tiers: May: 500M tokens, June: 1.25B tokens, July: 2.5B tokens, Aug: 2.5B tokens (step-up schedule with peak in July).
- Discount mix: baseline per-token public price less 18% for commit volume, plus an additional 3% loyalty rebate if annualized run rate stays above 1.5B/month after Q3 true-up.
- Surge buffer: 20% burst allowance within committed month before overage pricing applies; true-up at month end will convert sustained overages into next-month increment or bill as overage at committed rate + 12%.
- Invoice cadence: monthly invoicing with an estimated invoice on the 5th business day for prior month usage; true-up adjustments on the same invoice where possible.

Ask: please confirm whether BrightCart’s finance team needs invoice dates aligned with your existing vendor cycle (we can shift to the 10th if that helps). Also confirm whether the 20% surge allowance is sufficient for your anticipated launch-day burst.

Thanks — I’ve attached the spreadsheet with the token forecast and a short SLA-exception cover letter we discussed.

— Evelyn

Rajat — great questions. Quick answers inline: 

1) Baseline: $0.00075 per token for the hosted text-generation SKU (same as published on our pricing page). The 18% discount maps to an effective $0.000615/token for committed volume. I added a worksheet in the spreadsheet showing month-by-month effective unit cost.

2) Loyalty rebate mechanics: operationally we apply the 3% as a monthly credit on invoices once you hit the annualized threshold at the quarterly true-up. We can also structure as an annual rebate if procurement requires it; either is fine but credits on invoices simplify cashflow.

3) Invoice timing: we can set invoice date to the 10th and term to net 30 without impacting the commit economics. I’ve noted that with Finance — Marcus is looping on collections flow and SLA exceptions.

About the launch-week spike: the 60% short-duration spike fits within our 20% surge buffer only if you absorb some of it into the May commit step-up (i.e., move part of May’s contingency into an early June temporary uplift) — otherwise the sustained portion beyond 20% will be billed as overage. Do you have flexibility to reallocate tokens in the month-to-month true-up?

If procurement is okay with invoice-on-10th and credits for loyalty, I’ll get a revised term sheet and updated spreadsheet with an optional temporary uplift scenario for launch week.

— Evelyn
